page: The UpCloud PREMIUM-48xCPU-96GB is a compute-oriented virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with shared CPU allocation, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 400 GB of local SSD storage. No GPU accelerators are present in this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations place this server's compute capabilities in the top tier. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench rank in the top 10% of tested hardware, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 24,465.0 and a software compilation score of 61,453.0. Cryptographic and vector processing are supported by hardware-level instruction sets, including AVX-512 and AES, which contribute to strong encryption and database operation scores. Memory read bandwidth is strong, reaching up to 6,024.49 GB/sec for cached small blocks, though overall PassMark memory scores fall into the average tier.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the server prioritizes raw parallel processing power over massive memory capacity. This makes it highly cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads that do not require vast memory footprints, such as software compilation, text and image processing, and multi-threaded decompression. However, the shared CPU allocation model and lower memory-per-core ratio represent a tradeoff for memory-intensive database systems or large-scale LLM text generation, where performance falls into the average to weak categories. It is best suited for high-throughput web serving, parallel CI/CD pipelines, and CPU-heavy batch processing.
